title: The Four Noble Truths
objective: After this level you can explain the Buddha's diagnosis of suffering, its cause in craving, and why he taught that it can end.
summary: In his first sermon at Sarnath, the Buddha taught the Four Noble Truths: suffering, its cause in craving, its end in nirvana, and the Eightfold Path that leads there.

cards.headline: The Buddha's first sermon fits in four sentences.
cards.body: Buddhists call them the Four Noble Truths. Think of a visit to a doctor: what's wrong, what causes it, whether it can be cured, and the treatment.

cards.headline: Five old companions at a deer park
cards.body: After his enlightenment, the Buddha went to the Deer Park at Sarnath. His audience was five ascetics, his former companions from the years of self-denial. Buddhists call that first sermon setting the wheel of the dharma, the teaching, in motion. At its heart were four truths.

cards.headline: Truth one: nothing fully satisfies
cards.body: The first truth is dukkha, usually translated "suffering". It is wider than pain. Dukkha carries a sense of uneasiness or dissatisfaction, rooted in a world that keeps changing. Think of the best meal of your life: even while you eat it, it is ending. Buddhists see dukkha running through the whole cycle of rebirth, samsara.

cards.headline: Cause, cure, treatment
cards.body: The second truth names the cause: craving (tanha), a thirst that keeps reaching for more. The third says suffering can cease, and its cessation is nirvana. The fourth gives the way there: the Eightfold Path. That is the logic of the whole teaching. If suffering has a cause, removing the cause can end it.
cards.callout: Suffering, its cause (craving), its end (nirvana), the path

cards.headline: The Four Noble Truths: the takeaways
learned: The first sermon at Sarnath set the "wheel of the dharma" moving
Nirvana ends suffering; the Eightfold Path leads there

questions.prompt: According to the second noble truth, what is the origin of suffering?

options.label: A lack of wealth
options.rationale: The cause is craving, not poverty.

questions.explanation: The second truth: the origin of suffering is craving, tanha.

questions.prompt: Why did the Buddha teach that suffering can come to an end?

options.label: It fades by itself over time
options.rationale: It ends when its cause is removed.

options.label: Its cause, craving, can be removed
Only the rich and powerful suffer
options.rationale: Dukkha runs through all of samsara.

options.label: Every new life is better than the last
options.rationale: The answer lies in ending craving.

questions.explanation: Suffering has a cause, craving. Remove the cause and suffering ceases: that cessation is nirvana.

questions.prompt: Who heard the Buddha's first sermon at Sarnath?

options.label: His father's royal court
options.rationale: The sermon was at Sarnath, to five ascetics.

options.label: Five ascetics who had shared his years of self-denial
A great crowd of monks and nuns
options.rationale: The five would become the first monks.

questions.explanation: He taught five ascetics, his former companions from his six years of self-denial, at the Deer Park.
